editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Job, session and batch modes, closing sessions to cut wait times for later users, and batch mode helping when all jobs are known up front all match the English, and nothing is hallucinated. The problem is register: the page ends statements in formal 합니다체 (설명합니다, 활용합니다, 확인할 수 있습니다, 시작합니다) and only switches to 해요체 in imperatives (참고하세요, 알아보세요). editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The shot-count caveat in [27], the negation that a single randomization gives no benefit in [32]/[33], and every row of the shape table in [47] all match the English. editor_note: In entry [40], "equal, up to single-qubit gates" is calqued as "단일 qubit 게이트까지 동일합니다". A Korean reader takes that as "identical down to and including single-qubit gates", which is the opposite of the intended "equal, ignoring single-qubit gates". That flips the uniqueness rule for noise-learning boxes and misleads the learner, so the page fails. There are smaller problems too. The whole page uses 합니다체 (보여줍니다, 개발되었습니다) instead of 해요체. Entry [52] has the awkward "기댓값 (기대값: 1.0)". "task" is rendered as both 태스크 [24] and 작업 [45][48], and 작업 is also used for "job".

examples.why: 'up to' means 'ignoring' here. The Korean '까지' reads as 'even including single-qubit gates', which inverts the equivalence criterion.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the editable-mode caveat in [32] and the debug/release-mode explanation in [30]. The terms are correct and consistent: 편집 가능 모드, 디버그 모드, 릴리스 모드, 저장소, 클론, 린팅. The only problem is register. Most of the page uses the formal -ㅂ니다 ending (합쇼체: 알아봅니다, 있습니다, 생성합니다, 설치합니다), and a few entries switch to -세요 (사용하세요, 빌드하세요). The house convention is 해요체, so a native editor would convert it for consistency. No learner would be misled.

examples.why: This uses the formal 합쇼체 ending (-ㅂ니다), but the convention is 해요체. The same pattern appears in [0], [6], [12], [21], [22], [23], [24] and [28].

examples.source: Navigate to your project directory and create a minimal environment with only Python installed in it.

examples.why: The step-by-step instructions switch between declarative -ㅂ니다 here and imperative -세요 in [19] and [30]. Using 해요체 imperatives throughout would read more naturally and match the house style.

editor_note: Faithful, natural 해요체 throughout. The load()/loads() and dump()/dumps() file-versus-string distinctions are kept correctly (파일 이름을 받는 `load()`, 문자열로 내보내거나), and the exploratory-phase caveat survives as 탐색적 개발 단계.

The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. Instructions (-세요) follow the 해요체 convention, but every declarative sentence switches to formal 합니다체: 생성됩니다 and 할당할 수 있습니다 in [3], 받게 됩니다 and 표시됩니다 in [11], 표시됩니다 in [15], and 표시되지 않습니다 and 액세스할 수 있습니다 in [16]. These should be 해요체 (생성돼요, 받게 돼요, 표시돼요, 표시되지 않아요, 있어요). [16] also says 해당 사용자 twice in one clause, which reads as a stiff calque.

The example scenario matches its setup: Fatima/Ravi/Amyra map to the ml/finance access groups, QR-common is shared, and the job.delete custom rule is intact. Nothing here would mislead a learner. The page does not follow the project's 해요체 convention, though. Statements are in formal 합니다체 (e.g. 설명하며…제공합니다, 확인합니다, 생성합니다), mixed with -세요 imperatives. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The qubit-vs-data-volume caveat and the "not yet implemented" caveat in [42] both survive, and the benchmark table matches the English. The prose uses 합니다체 (습니다/합니다) consistently instead of the project's 해요체. There are also several inconsistencies: "quantum-enhanced" appears as both 양자 향상 [14] and 양자 강화 [24][31–34]; "interleaving half circles" is the calque 인터리빙 반원 in [12] but 맞물린 반원 in [20]; the product name is kept in English in [10]/[20] but partly translated as "Singularity 머신 러닝 - 분류" in [40]/[60], which also gives both 머신러닝 and 머신 러닝. Two smaller slips: the title in [1] renders "by Multiverse Computing" as "을 통한" ("via"), and [15] calques "accepts hyperparameters" as 하이퍼파라미터를 허용합니다.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. Product names and UI labels (ENVS, + ADD, Install) are kept verbatim, and the setup steps match the English one for one. There is one small softening in the regional-availability note [10]: the English says flatly that OVHcloud AI notebooks "are not available" in some regions, such as the US. The Korean "이용하지 못할 수 있습니다" means "may not be usable", which turns a definite fact into a possibility. The warning still reaches the reader, so it is not misleading enough to fail, but it should be restored to a definite statement.

examples.source: OVHcloud AI notebooks are not available in some regions, such as the United States.
examples.translation: OVHcloud AI 노트북은 미국 등 일부 지역에서는 이용하지 못할 수 있습니다.

examples.why: The hedge '-ㄹ 수 있습니다' makes a definite unavailability sound only possible, which weakens the caveat.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. Conditions, version pins (qiskit<1, qiskit>=0.45,<1, qiskit-terra>=1.0) and caveats all come through intact, and 호환성 파괴 변경, 전이적 의존성 and 제약 조건 파일 are used consistently. There are a few small slips. [96] renders 'Python packaging authority', which is the name of an organization (PyPA), as '패키징 권한' ('permission'). [79] drops 'tried' ('we have tried to make Qiskit fail…' becomes a flat '구현했습니다'), which makes the claim stronger than the source. In [145] the subject of '이것도 … 일부이므로' is unclear: it reads as if the reinstall itself is part of the setuptools build process. [103] loses 'rest assured', so the note no longer reassures the reader. Prose is mostly 합니다체 rather than 해요체, which is normal for Korean docs but differs from the stated convention.

editor_note: In entry [10], the relative clause attaches "공식 Qiskit 라이브러리를 기반으로 한 여러 도전적인 코드 문제를 포함하는" to HumanEval. The Korean therefore says the original HumanEval benchmark is built on Qiskit libraries, when the English says this about QHE and QHE Hard. That is a false claim a learner could pick up, so the page fails. The register also changes partway through: it uses 해요체 up to about [44], then switches to 합니다체 from [46] and stays there from [66] to the end (…입니다, …있습니다). Smaller problems: "trained" is rendered both as 훈련 and as 학습 ([4]/[134] vs [136]/[140]); [126] is ungrammatical ("사용하기 위해 최신 권장 모델입니다"); and [11] and [100] are stiff calques.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall, but in [15] the qualifier "breaking" is dropped. "qiskit<2" now reads as guaranteeing a version with no API changes at all ("API 변경 사항이 없는"), when the English only promises no breaking changes. "private" appears first as the wrong word "개인(private)" and then as "비공개" in [10], and "release" alternates between 출시 and 릴리스 across the page. [4] opens with the calqued "API 변경 사항의 하위 호환성 파괴는 … 적용됩니다", and [14] adds "향후" (future), which the source doesn't have.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Version bounds (Rust 1.91 이상), log levels and their default (`warn`), RPM names and build steps all match the English, and nothing would mislead a learner. There are two things a native editor would still change. First, the whole page uses 하십시오체 endings (~입니다, ~합니다, 설치합니다) instead of the project's 해요체 convention. Second, [13] turns "Rust unknown targets" into the literal "Rust 알 수 없는 타겟", which reads as "targets Rust cannot recognize" instead of the "*-unknown-*" target-triple category.

examples.source: Clang (`clang-tools-extra`) for Rust unknown targets/cross compilations
examples.translation: Rust 알 수 없는 타겟/크로스 컴파일을 위해서는 Clang(`clang-tools-extra`)
examples.suggested: Rust의 unknown 타겟(예: *-unknown-*) 빌드나 크로스 컴파일에는 Clang(`clang-tools-extra`)
examples.why: 'unknown' is part of a target-triple name, not an adjective. Translating it as 알 수 없는 turns it into a calque that suggests Rust can't recognize the target.

examples.source: ...is a vendor-agnostic library for high-performance compute (HPC) systems...
examples.translation: ...벤더 독립적 라이브러리입니다. ... 동작합니다. ... 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: ...벤더 독립적 라이브러리예요. ... 동작해요. ... 제공해요.
examples.why: The whole file uses 하십시오체 (~입니다/~합니다) instead of the 해요체 register this locale is meant to use.

editor_note: I found no misleading passages. The TTL rules ([16], [17], [23]) and the close/cancel caveats in [25] match the English. There are three minor problems. "Interactive TTL" is written as 대화형 in [17]/[20] but 인터랙티브 in [28]. "Primitive jobs" in [6] becomes 기본 작업, which reads as "basic jobs" and doesn't match 기본 요소, the term used for primitive in [32]/[34]. Also in [6], "examples of working with batches" becomes 배치 작업 예시들, which is ambiguous and reads like "batch job examples".

examples.source: including its interactive and max TTL
examples.translation: 인터랙티브 및 최대 TTL을 포함하여
examples.suggested: 대화형 및 최대 TTL을 포함하여
examples.why: Entries [17] and [20] use 대화형 TTL for the same concept. Switching to 인터랙티브 here is inconsistent.

examples.source: Use batch mode to submit multiple primitive jobs simultaneously.
examples.translation: 배치 모드를 사용하여 여러 기본 작업을 동시에 제출할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 배치 모드를 사용하면 여러 프리미티브(기본 요소) 작업을 동시에 제출할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 기본 작업 reads as 'basic tasks', so the learner can't tell these are Sampler/Estimator primitive jobs. It is also inconsistent with 기본 요소 in [32]/[34].

examples.source: Following are examples of working with batches.
examples.translation: 다음은 배치 작업 예시들입니다.
examples.suggested: 다음은 배치를 다루는 예시입니다.
examples.why: 배치 작업 is easy to read as 'batch jobs' rather than 'working with batches', and the plural 예시들 is a calque of the English plural.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The TTL behaviour, the end-of-session conditions (queued jobs cancelled or failed vs. running jobs finishing) and the status descriptions all match the English. However, all declarative prose uses the formal -습니다 ending (e.g. 닫힙니다, 수락하지 않습니다), while imperatives use -세요, so the page misses the 해요체 convention. Two smaller issues: [30] 'with priority' became the awkward '우선순위로 계속 실행됩니다' (more natural: '우선적으로'), and 'classical' is rendered '클래식' ([48], [49], [52]) where Korean quantum texts normally say '고전'.

examples.source: continues to run queued jobs with priority
examples.translation: 대기 중인 작업은 우선순위로 계속 실행됩니다
examples.suggested: 대기 중인 작업은 우선적으로 계속 실행해요
examples.why: '우선순위로 실행' is a calque that reads oddly; '우선적으로' carries the intended meaning.

examples.source: frequent communication between classical and quantum resources
examples.translation: 클래식 리소스와 양자 리소스 간의 빈번한 통신
examples.suggested: 고전 리소스와 양자 리소스 간의 빈번한 통신
examples.why: The conventional Korean term for classical (as opposed to quantum) computing is '고전'. '클래식' is recognizable but non-standard.

examples.source: Any jobs that are running will finish, but jobs still queued are failed.
examples.translation: 실행 중인 작업은 완료되지만, 아직 대기 중인 작업은 실패 처리됩니다.
examples.suggested: 실행 중인 작업은 완료되지만, 아직 대기 중인 작업은 실패 처리돼요.
examples.why: The whole page uses -습니다 formal endings instead of the project's 해요체 convention.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, with no drift or hallucination: the job_id/QiskitRuntimeService.job retrieval steps, the three-month created_after filter and the datetime requirement all match the English, and the 해요체 register holds. There are two small naturalness problems. In [8], "커널 재시작 간에도" is a calque of "across kernel restarts"; "커널을 재시작한 후에도" reads more naturally. In [6], the last sentence joins two clauses with "저장하고, ... 가져올 수 있어" and the result is a clumsy run-on.

examples.source: Use this feature to continue quantum programs across kernel restarts and review past results.
examples.translation: 이 기능을 사용하여 커널 재시작 간에도 양자 프로그램을 계속 실행하고 이전 결과를 검토할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 이 기능을 사용하면 커널을 재시작한 후에도 양자 프로그램을 이어서 실행하고 이전 결과를 검토할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '재시작 간에도' is a literal calque of 'across restarts' and is not idiomatic Korean.

examples.source: To avoid loss of data, you can save results to file and retrieve results of past jobs from IBM Quantum so your next session can continue where you left off.
examples.translation: 데이터 손실을 방지하기 위해 결과를 파일에 저장하고, IBM Quantum®에서 이전 작업의 결과를 가져올 수 있어 다음 세션에서 이전 작업을 이어서 진행할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 데이터 손실을 막으려면 결과를 파일에 저장하거나 IBM Quantum®에서 이전 작업의 결과를 가져오면 돼요. 그러면 다음 세션에서 중단한 지점부터 이어서 진행할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The chained '저장하고, ... 가져올 수 있어 ... 할 수 있습니다' makes a stiff run-on with 'can' repeated. Splitting it into two sentences reads more naturally.

editor_note: Nothing on this page would mislead a learner. The node limits (최대 2개 / 최대 4개의 작업), the Python 3.11+ requirement, the plan-eligibility caveat and the workloads-table caveat are all rendered correctly. The main problem is register: declarative sentences use formal 합니다/습니다 throughout (제공합니다, 포함됩니다, 있습니다) instead of the project's 해요체, so the imperatives (확인하세요, 참고해 주세요) sit in a different register from the rest. There are also two small calques: '3.11 이상을 필요로 합니다' and '일부 튜토리얼을 시험해 보세요'.

examples.source: Qiskit Serverless provides a simple interface to run workloads across quantum-classical resources.
examples.translation: Qiskit Serverless는 양자-고전 리소스 전반에서 워크로드를 실행할 수 있는 간단한 인터페이스를 제공합니다.
examples.suggested: Qiskit Serverless는 양자-고전 리소스 전반에서 워크로드를 실행할 수 있는 간단한 인터페이스를 제공해요.
examples.why: The page is in formal 합니다체 throughout, but the project convention is 해요체. It is applied consistently, so this is minor.

examples.source: These packages require `python` 3.11+.
examples.translation: 이 패키지들은 `python` 3.11 이상을 필요로 합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 패키지를 사용하려면 `python` 3.11 이상이 필요해요.
examples.why: '~을 필요로 하다' is a calque of English 'require'. A Korean technical writer would say '~이 필요하다'.

examples.source: Try out some tutorials.
examples.translation: 일부 튜토리얼을 시험해 보세요.
examples.suggested: [튜토리얼](...)도 따라 해 보세요.
examples.why: '일부' is a literal rendering of 'some' and '시험해 보세요' reads stiffly. It sounds like machine translation.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The account, billing and trial conditions in [13]-[23] are carried over correctly, including "*요금이 청구되지 않지만*". The main problem is register. Nearly every statement ends in 하십시오체 (-합니다/-있습니다), and [8] uses the humble "도움을 드릴", [16] "귀하의" and [10] "계신가요", where the project convention is 해요체. There is also one slightly softened caveat: in [19], "you will likely lose access" became "잃을 수 있습니다" ("may lose"), which weakens the warning.

examples.source: Our team includes technical experts ready to assist across this full range of topics.
examples.translation: 저희 팀에는 이 모든 주제에 걸쳐 도움을 드릴 준비가 된 기술 전문가들이 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 저희 팀에는 이 모든 주제를 도와줄 수 있는 기술 전문가가 있어요.
examples.why: The humble 드리 and 하십시오체 ending break the 해요체 convention.

examples.source: (Note that you will likely lose access at the end of the trial).
examples.translation: (체험 종료 시 액세스를 잃을 수 있습니다).
examples.suggested: (체험 기간이 끝나면 액세스 권한을 잃을 가능성이 높아요).
examples.why: "likely" became "may", which softens the caveat so losing access sounds less probable than the source says.

examples.source: your country is on the Personal use availability list
examples.translation: 귀하의 국가가 [개인 사용 가용성] 목록에 있다면
examples.suggested: 사용자의 국가가 [개인 사용 가능 국가] 목록에 있다면
examples.why: 귀하 is stiff, formal-letter register, and 개인 사용 가용성 is a calque.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing would mislead a learner. The billing caveats in [19] and [21] (charged only when a Pay-As-You-Go instance sends QPU workloads; use an Open Plan or other free-plan instance for no-cost use, if you have one) are kept exactly. The file's declarative sentences use the formal 합니다체 (e.g. "안내입니다", "생성합니다", "권장합니다") instead of the project's 해요체 convention. The "Recommendations" list in [24] mixes noun-style items ("비용 관리하기", "알아보기") with 해요체 imperatives ("따라 … 실행해 보세요", "시도해 보세요"). "튜토리얼을 시도해 보세요" is also a calque of "Try a tutorial".

examples.source: Try a [tutorial](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/tutorials).
examples.translation: [튜토리얼](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/tutorials)을 시도해 보세요.
examples.suggested: [튜토리얼](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/tutorials) 따라해 보기.
examples.why: '시도해 보세요' is a literal calque of 'try'. The list also mixes noun-style items (…하기) with imperatives, so all items should use the same form.

examples.source: This guide is for entities who want to upgrade ...
examples.translation: ... 업그레이드하려는 사용자를 위한 안내입니다.
examples.suggested: ... 업그레이드하려는 사용자를 위한 안내예요.
examples.why: Formal 합니다체 is used across the file (also [8] 생성합니다, [22] 권장합니다), but the project convention is 해요체.

examples.source: [Manage cost](/guides/manage-cost) when using the Pay-As-You-Go Plan.
examples.translation: Pay-As-You-Go Plan 사용 시 [비용 관리](/guides/manage-cost)하기.
examples.suggested: Pay-As-You-Go Plan 사용 시 [비용을 관리](/guides/manage-cost)하는 방법 알아보기.
examples.why: Splitting the link text from '하기' ('[비용 관리]하기') is awkward in Korean.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing here would mislead a learner. The public-versus-private contrast in [5]-[7] is carried over exactly, including "공용 네트워크를 통해서만 액세스할 수 있습니다" for the website. Two small wording slips remain. [10] translates "Private" as "가상 사설 클라우드", but every other entry uses "프라이빗" (가상 프라이빗 엔드포인트, 프라이빗 백본, 프라이빗 연결). In [4], IBM Cloud's Korean docs call "availability zones" "가용성 구역" (가용성 영역 is used here).

examples.source: [Create a Virtual Private Cloud](...)
examples.translation: [가상 사설 클라우드 생성](...)
examples.suggested: [가상 프라이빗 클라우드 생성](...)
examples.why: Every other entry renders "Private" as 프라이빗, so this one should match.

examples.source: spans all availability zones of your VPC
examples.translation: VPC의 모든 가용성 영역에 걸쳐 있는
examples.suggested: VPC의 모든 가용성 구역에 걸쳐 있는
examples.why: IBM Cloud's Korean docs use 가용성 구역 for availability zone. The current term is recognizable but not the platform convention.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and consistently uses 해요체-free 합니다체 teaching prose, but a few things need fixing. In [39], the qualifier 'not necessarily something actual' becomes '실제 현실이 아니라', which states more than the English does. Four DefinitionTooltips were left in English: stochastic [75], associative [88], composition [88] and commutative [91]. 'associative/commutative' are rendered as '결합 연산'/'교환 연산', and '교환 연산' reads like a swap operation. 'probabilistic state' is split between 확률적 상태 and 확률 상태 ([79], [86]).

examples.source: probabilistic states describe knowledge or belief, not necessarily something actual
examples.translation: 확률적 상태는 실제 현실이 아니라 지식이나 믿음을 서술하며
examples.suggested: 확률적 상태는 반드시 실제의 무언가가 아니라 지식이나 믿음을 서술하며
examples.why: The 'not necessarily' hedge is dropped, so the claim becomes absolute: probabilistic states are never something actual.

examples.source: definition="Stochastic roughly means random. A stochastic matrix represents a random process."
examples.translation: definition="Stochastic roughly means random. A stochastic matrix represents a random process."
examples.suggested: definition="stochastic은 대략 '무작위'를 뜻합니다. 확률 행렬은 무작위 과정을 나타냅니다."
examples.why: The tooltip text is untranslated. The same happens for associative/composition [88] and commutative [91].

examples.source: it is not a commutative operation
examples.translation: <DefinitionTooltip ...>교환</DefinitionTooltip> 연산은 아닙니다
examples.suggested: 교환 법칙이 성립하는 연산은 아닙니다
examples.why: '교환 연산' can be read as a swap operation. The standard phrasing is '교환 법칙이 성립하는' (and '결합 법칙이 성립하는' in [88]).

examples.source: the probabilistic state that is generated
examples.translation: 생성되는 확률 상태
examples.suggested: 생성되는 확률적 상태
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 확률적 상태. [79] and [86] switch to 확률 상태.

examples.source: we might happen to know with certainty that it is set to high
examples.translation: 우리는 스위치가 고속으로 설정되어 있다는 것을 확실히 알고 있고
examples.suggested: 스위치가 고속으로 설정되어 있다는 것을 확실히 알고 있을 수 있고
examples.why: The hypothetical 'might happen to' is dropped, so the example reads as a flat assertion of fact.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still change several things. 'course' and 'lesson' are both rendered as 강의, which produces "이 강의의 세 번째 강의" in [44], and in [10] "within a given lesson" became "각 섹션", which narrows the scope. Some calques read stiffly: "표본의 분수" for "fraction of samples" should be 비율, "신선한 복사본" in [50] clashes with "새로운 복사본" in [35], and "연산들의 수열" uses the numeric-sequence term for a sequence of operations. [3] is clumsy ("…싶으시다면, 이를 적극 권장합니다."), and "composing" is rendered as 작성하는 instead of 조합하는.

examples.source: which is the third lesson in this course
examples.translation: 이 강의의 세 번째 강의인 [양자 회로] 강의에서
examples.suggested: 이 코스의 세 번째 레슨인 [양자 회로] 레슨에서 ... 단일 qubit 유니터리 연산들을 조합하는 실험
examples.why: Course and lesson are both 강의, so 'the third 강의 of this 강의' is confusing. 'composing' is also rendered as 작성 (writing) instead of 조합/합성.

examples.source: all code appearing within a given lesson in this course is expected to be run sequentially
examples.translation: 이 강의의 각 섹션에서 나타나는 모든 코드는 순차적으로 실행될 것으로 예상된다는 점을 주목하세요.
examples.suggested: 이 코스의 각 레슨에 나오는 코드는 모두 순서대로 실행한다고 가정한다는 점에 유의하세요.
examples.why: 'lesson' became 섹션, which narrows the scope of the sequential-execution assumption. The phrasing is also a stiff calque.

examples.source: the fraction of samples for each possibility is likely to get closer and closer to the corresponding probability
examples.translation: 각 가능성에 대한 표본의 분수가 해당 확률에 더 가까워질 가능성이 높습니다.
examples.suggested: 각 결과가 나온 샘플의 비율이 해당 확률에 점점 더 가까워질 가능성이 높습니다.
examples.why: 분수 is a literal calque of 'fraction'. The idiomatic word is 비율. The entry also switches between 샘플 and 표본.

examples.source: (using a fresh copy of the state each time)
examples.translation: (매번 상태의 신선한 복사본을 사용합니다.)
examples.suggested: (매번 상태의 새로운 복사본을 사용합니다.)
examples.why: 신선한 is a food-style calque of 'fresh' and does not match 새로운 복사본, used for the same phrase in [35].

examples.source: If you wish to run these implementations yourself, which is strongly encouraged, consult the Install Qiskit page
examples.translation: 직접 이러한 구현들을 실행해보고 싶으시다면, 이를 적극 권장합니다. [IBM Quantum 문서]의 [Qiskit 설치] 페이지를 참고하여…
examples.suggested: 이 구현들을 직접 실행해 보기를 적극 권장해요. Qiskit 설정 방법은 [IBM Quantum 문서]의 [Qiskit 설치] 페이지를 참고하세요.
examples.why: The English relative clause is calqued into a broken conditional ('if you want to…, we strongly encourage it'). It also uses the honorific 싶으시다면.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The 1-3 / 4-5 references, the "at most two dimensions" advice and both value-map examples all match the English. The problems are a typo and some translationese. In [7], "near-term quantum advantage" is rendered "근기 양자 이점", a typo for 근시일 내/단기 (근기 means stamina). "Guiding priorities" appears twice as "지도 우선순위", which reads as "map priorities". Several calques remain: "성공이 어떻게 보이는지" [31], "목표의 발전자" [22], "다시 방문하고" [60], the causative "…중요하게 만듭니다" [12], and "출시" (product release) for an initiative's launch [59].

examples.source: to a focus area that targets near-term quantum advantage
examples.translation: 근기 양자 이점을 목표로 하는 집중 영역에 맞추세요
examples.suggested: 가까운 시일 내 양자 우위(이점)를 목표로 하는 집중 영역에 맞추세요
examples.why: '근기' is a typo, and the word means stamina/perseverance, not near-term. A reader can still guess the intent, so this stays minor.

examples.source: This makes it important to have guiding priorities and clear criteria for success.
examples.translation: 이는 지도 우선순위와 명확한 성공 기준을 갖는 것이 중요하게 만듭니다.
examples.suggested: 그래서 방향을 잡아 줄 우선순위와 명확한 성공 기준을 세워 두는 것이 중요해요.
examples.why: The English causative is calqued ('~을 중요하게 만듭니다'), and '지도 우선순위' is ambiguous because 지도 can also mean map. The same term comes back in [31].

examples.source: Map each goal to a benefit to identify advancers of the goal.
examples.translation: 각 목표를 혜택에 매핑하여 목표의 발전자를 식별하세요.
examples.suggested: 각 목표를 혜택과 연결해 목표 달성을 앞당길 수단을 파악하세요.
examples.why: '목표의 발전자' is a literal rendering that doesn't work in Korean. It reads as 'the developer of the goal'.

examples.source: to decide what success looks like
examples.translation: 성공이 어떻게 보이는지를 결정할 때입니다
examples.suggested: 무엇을 성공으로 볼지 정할 때입니다
examples.why: This is a literal calque of the English idiom 'what success looks like'.

examples.source: You may need to revisit your engagement model
examples.translation: 참여 모델을 다시 방문하고

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. I found no drift or invented claims. There are some native-editor fixes. In [29], "Together," became the broken fragment "이 함께,", and [26] contains the calques "IBM QIC 주변의 결과적인 커뮤니티" and "더 경쟁력 있는 신청을 촉진할 수 있습니다". In [22], "enabling technologies" was rendered as the odd "가능 기술". The page is also written in the 합니다체 declarative (입니다/합니다) everywhere, not the project's 해요체 convention. Only [12] "함께하세요" matches it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the threshold logic in [11] and [14] (Cp^2, p < 1/C), the doubly- versus singly-exponential contrast in [20]-[21], and the 0.1%-1% surface-code estimate in [22]. Nothing would mislead a learner. There are four minor issues. In [14] a stray `$` merges two sentences ("시작합니다$.p < ... = 1/C$라고"), which drops the sentence break and puts a period inside the math. In [25] "도움을 해 주세요" is ungrammatical. In [21] "인수만큼 최대로 증가" is stiff. The page also uses 합니다체 throughout rather than the 해요체 convention.

examples.why: A misplaced `$` puts the sentence-ending period inside the math and runs the two sentences together, so the page renders '.p < ...'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats in [24] and the RSA250/number field sieve facts in [17]. However, "The answer is yes" in [24] comes out as the ungrammatical "답은 그렇습니다입니다". Math delimiters have drifted around punctuation in [9] ("예를 들어$,12$", "이며$,12$") and [20] ("출력$:N$"), which will render wrongly. The whole page is written in 합니다체 instead of the 해요체 convention, and [17] has a calqued word order ("가장 빠른 알려진 알고리즘").

examples.source: The answer is yes.
examples.translation: 답은 그렇습니다입니다.
examples.suggested: 답은 '그렇다'예요.
examples.why: Two predicates are stacked (그렇습니다 + 입니다). The result is ungrammatical, and a native writer would never produce it.

examples.source: The fastest known algorithm for factoring large integers
examples.translation: 큰 정수를 소인수분해하기 위한 가장 빠른 알려진 알고리즘은

examples.translation: 이러한 믿음은 잘못된 것입니다.
examples.suggested: 이런 믿음은 잘못된 거예요.
examples.why: The whole page uses formal 합니다체 instead of the project's 해요체 convention.

editor_note: Entry [100] is a copy of [99]'s translation, so the lesson's closing lead-in ("let's apply these formulas to the same state we considered above") is gone and the extension claim is repeated. Entry [41] also drifts. "This description doesn't include Bob's measurement outcome" became "doesn't include the assumption that Bob measured his qubit", which borrows the point [42] goes on to argue. Terminology is split: reduced state is both 축약 상태 and 환산 상태, partial trace is both 부분 대각합 and 부분 트레이스, and traced out is both 추적 소거 and 트레이스 아웃. "Square matrix" is given as 제곱 행렬 (squared matrix) rather than 정사각 행렬. [36] and [80] have broken sentence structure, and [46] drops "Suppose", so the assumption reads as a statement of fact.

examples.source: To finish the lesson, let's apply these formulas to the same state we considered above.
examples.translation: 이 함수들의 블록 행렬 설명은 큐비트보다 큰 시스템으로 자연스럽고 직접적인 방식으로 확장될 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 수업을 마무리하며, 앞에서 살펴본 같은 상태에 이 공식들을 적용해 봅시다.
examples.why: This is the translation of entry [99], not [100]. The lead-in to the worked example is lost and an unrelated claim is repeated.

examples.source: this description of the state of Alice's qubit doesn't include Bob's measurement outcome; we're ignoring Bob altogether.
examples.translation: 고립된 Alice의 큐비트의 상태에 대한 이 밀도 행렬 설명은 Bob이 자신의 큐비트를 측정했다는 가정을 포함하지 않습니다
examples.suggested: Alice의 큐비트 상태에 대한 이 설명에는 Bob의 측정 결과가 포함되어 있지 않아요. 우리는 Bob을 완전히 무시하고 있어요.
examples.why: The source says the measurement outcome is left out. The translation instead says the assumption of a measurement is left out, which states [42]'s conclusion early and changes the claim.

examples.source: the *reduced states* of the systems
examples.translation: *환산 상태(reduced state)*
examples.suggested: *축약 상태*
examples.why: The heading and entries [1] through [45] use 축약 상태. From [68] on the file switches to 환산 상태, and in [65] and [95] partial trace becomes 부분 트레이스 and traced out becomes 트레이스 아웃, where [63] used 추적 소거.

examples.source: $N$ and $M$ are square matrices of the appropriate sizes
examples.translation: 적절한 크기의 제곱 행렬입니다
examples.suggested: 적절한 크기의 정사각 행렬입니다
examples.why: 제곱 행렬 means a squared matrix. The standard term for a square matrix is 정사각 행렬.

examples.source: and he would obtain the outcome $1$ with probability
examples.translation: 그리고 그는 결과 1을 확률로 얻을 것입니다
examples.suggested: 그리고 다음 확률로 결과 $1$을 얻게 됩니다
examples.why: The sentence is garbled. "다음" is missing, so it no longer points to the formula that follows.

editor_note: In [20], the marketing term "next best action recommendations" is translated as "관련 차선책 추천". 차선책 means a second-best fallback, so the sentence now says quantum improves recommendations of fallback options. This is semantic drift, and it is why the page fails. In [64], O'Meara's question is misparsed: "가스를 태우는 발전소에서 수천 킬로미터 떨어진 곳에서 만들어진 에너지" says the energy was made thousands of km away from the gas plant, not by a distant gas plant. Smaller slips: "quantum dynamics" becomes 양자 역학 (quantum mechanics) in [72], "many years" is inflated to 수십 년간 in [40], and "verification and validation" is merged into one word, 소프트웨어 검증, in [50].

examples.line_approx: Integrated classical–quantum solutions may improve customer profiling...
examples.source: relevant next best action recommendations
examples.translation: 관련 차선책 추천
examples.suggested: 적절한 차선 행동(next best action) 추천 → better: 고객별 최적의 다음 행동(next best action) 추천
examples.why: 차선책 means a second-best alternative. The English term means the best next action for each customer, so the translation turns the meaning around.

examples.line_approx: Why do you have to get energy from thousands of kilometers away...
examples.source: Why do you have to get energy from thousands of kilometers away that was made in the power plant burning gas?
examples.translation: 왜 가스를 태우는 발전소에서 수천 킬로미터 떨어진 곳에서 만들어진 에너지를 받아야 할까요?
examples.suggested: 왜 수천 킬로미터 떨어진, 가스를 태우는 발전소에서 만든 에너지를 받아야 할까요?
examples.why: The word order makes the energy come from a place far from the gas plant, not from the distant gas plant itself.

examples.line_approx: Simulating quantum dynamics to advance materials discovery
examples.source: Simulating quantum dynamics
examples.translation: 양자 역학 시뮬레이션
examples.suggested: 양자 동역학 시뮬레이션
examples.why: 양자 역학 is the usual term for quantum mechanics. Quantum dynamics is 양자 동역학.

examples.line_approx: The central role of the three-dimensional (3D) protein structure...

examples.translation: 수십 년간 연구되어 왔습니다
examples.suggested: 오랫동안 연구되어 왔습니다
examples.why: "Many years" is changed to "decades", which makes the claim stronger than the source.

examples.line_approx: The automotive industry could potentially benefit...

examples.translation: 소프트웨어 검증
examples.suggested: 소프트웨어 검증 및 확인(V&V)
examples.why: Verification and validation are two separate steps in engineering, and the translation merges them into one word.

editor_note: Nothing in the file would mislead a learner. The simulator-versus-hardware conclusion in [27] and the convergence caveat in [24] both match the English. Several terms are rendered inconsistently. 'error mitigation' is '오류 경감' in [19] but '오류 완화' in [27], 'ansatz' is left in English in [11] but written '앤사츠' in [22], 'optimizer' is '옵티마이저' in [18] but '최적화기' in [22], and the step headings mix 'Step 1/2/3' with '4단계'. There are also smaller problems. 'core energy' in [9] is rendered '핵심 에너지' ('key energy') where it should be 코어 에너지, [19] has the awkward doubled locative '후처리 섹션에서 아래에서', and the whole page uses the formal -습니다 style instead of the 해요체 convention, with honorific slips like '받으시면' in [30].

examples.source: This will return the core energy, single-electron energy, and two-electron energies as before.
examples.translation: 핵심 에너지, 단일 전자 에너지, 이중 전자 에너지를 반환합니다.
examples.suggested: 코어 에너지, 1전자 에너지, 2전자 에너지를 반환해요.
examples.why: In quantum chemistry, 'core energy' is the constant core/nuclear-repulsion term (코어 에너지). '핵심' means 'key/essential', so it reads as the wrong concept.

examples.source: only in the case of real hardware was error mitigation employed.
examples.translation: 실제 하드웨어의 경우에만 오류 완화가 적용되었기 때문으로 보입니다.
examples.suggested: Use one term, matching [19] ('오류 경감') or changing both to '오류 완화'.
examples.why: [19] renders 'error mitigation' as '오류 경감', so the same concept appears under two names within the page.

examples.source: trying other ansaetze, optimizers
examples.translation: 다른 앤사츠, 최적화기를 사용하거나
examples.suggested: 다른 ansatz나 옵티마이저를 사용하거나
examples.why: This conflicts with 'efficient_su2 ansatz' in [11] and '옵티마이저' in [18].

examples.source: The results of this output are discussed below in the post-processing section
examples.translation: 이 출력 결과는 후처리 섹션에서 아래에서 논의됩니다.
examples.suggested: 이 결과는 아래 후처리 섹션에서 다뤄요.
examples.why: The doubled locative ('섹션에서 아래에서') is a clumsy calque of the English word order.

examples.source: A score of 80% or higher will earn you a Credly badge
examples.translation: 80% 이상의 점수를 받으시면 Credly 배지를 받으실 수 있으며
examples.suggested: 80% 이상의 점수를 받으면 Credly 배지를 받을 수 있으며, 이메일로 자동 발송돼요.
examples.why: Honorific -시- forms, and the page-wide -습니다 style, depart from the 해요체 convention.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and the core terms are correct and consistent (해밀토니안, 페르미온/보손 연산자, 생성 및 소멸 연산자, 활성 공간, 기약 표현). The most visible problem is in entry [42]. The English has a typo, "statics" where "statistics" is meant, and the Korean copies it literally as "정역학" (statics, the branch of mechanics). Entry [19] already uses the correct word, 통계, so this should be changed to match. There are also some calques: "다른 정역학을 결과로 합니다" in [42], "해밀토니안을 원하는데" in [41], "아래에서 논평합니다" in [44], and "채움 수준" for "filling level" in [63]. A native editor would smooth these, but none of them misleads a learner.

examples.source: This results in different statics than would apply to a distinguishable or bosonic system.
examples.translation: 이는 구별 가능하거나 보손 시스템에 적용되는 것과는 다른 정역학을 결과로 합니다.
examples.suggested: 그 결과, 구별 가능한 입자나 보손 시스템과는 다른 통계를 따르게 됩니다.
examples.why: The source typo 'statics' (meant: statistics) is carried over as 정역학, which means mechanical statics. Entry [19] correctly says 통계. The phrase '결과로 합니다' is also a calque.

examples.source: We comment below on syntax considerations for other solutions.
examples.translation: 다른 솔루션의 구문 고려 사항에 대해서는 아래에서 논평합니다.
examples.suggested: 다른 솔루션을 사용할 때 고려할 구문 차이는 아래에서 설명합니다.
examples.why: '논평합니다' is too stiff and literal for 'comment' in a tutorial.

examples.source: We want a Hamiltonian, and this is often separated into energy of an electronic core ...
examples.translation: 해밀토니안을 원하는데, 이는 종종 전자 코어의 에너지...로 분리됩니다.
examples.suggested: 우리가 구하려는 해밀토니안은 흔히 전자 코어 에너지(...)...로 나뉩니다.
examples.why: '해밀토니안을 원하는데' is a direct calque of 'We want a Hamiltonian'.

examples.source: we take several orbitals near the filling level (valence and unoccupied)
examples.translation: 채움 수준 근처의 오비탈(원자가 및 비점유) 여러 개를 사용합니다.
examples.suggested: 전자가 채워진 최고 준위 근처의 오비탈(원자가 오비탈과 비점유 오비탈) 여러 개를 사용합니다.
examples.why: '채움 수준' is a literal coinage. Chemistry writing in Korean would use 준위 (energy level) phrasing, for example 페르미 준위 or HOMO/LUMO 근처.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere and nothing would mislead a learner: the 70% badge threshold, the limit on quiz attempts and the VQE/SQD split between quantum and classical work all come through intact. The whole page uses 합니다체 (e.g. 소개입니다, 활용합니다) instead of the 해요체 convention. Lesson 1's title leaves "Variational quantum eigensolver" in raw English, while the other lesson titles are translated (Krylov 양자 대각화, 샘플 기반 양자 대각화). A few calques read stiffly: "이는 ... SQD를 설명합니다" for "This describes SQD", "확장성" for "scaling" and "배급 네트워크" for "distribution networks".

examples.source: This describes sampling-based quantum diagonalization methods (SQD), some of the most exciting methods...
examples.translation: 이는 현재 양자 컴퓨팅 시대에서 가장 흥미로운 방법 중 하나인 샘플링 기반 양자 대각화 방법(SQD)을 설명합니다.
examples.suggested: 샘플링 기반 양자 대각화(SQD)가 바로 이런 경우로, 현재 양자 컴퓨팅 시대에서 가장 주목받는 방법 중 하나예요.
examples.why: This copies the English 'This describes' word for word. It reads as if the sentence explains SQD, when it actually says SQD is an example of this case.

examples.source: Lesson 1: Variational quantum eigensolver
examples.translation: 레슨 1: Variational quantum eigensolver
examples.suggested: 레슨 1: 변분 양자 고유값 해법(VQE)
examples.why: This is the only lesson title left untranslated, even though entry [7] already renders 'variational' as 변분.

examples.source: what factors determine the scaling of approaches
examples.translation: 접근 방식의 확장성을 결정하는 요인
examples.suggested: 접근 방식의 스케일링(규모에 따른 비용 증가)을 결정하는 요인
examples.why: 'Scaling' here means how cost grows with problem size, which is complexity scaling. 확장성 usually means 'scalability', which is close but not the same idea.

examples.source: The world is filled with problems...
examples.translation: 세상에는 ... 문제가 많이 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 세상에는 ... 문제가 많이 있어요.
examples.why: The whole file uses 합니다체 instead of the project's 해요체 convention.

editor_note: I found nothing that would mislead a learner. Conditions, quantities and caveats all match the English, including D = 2^{2n}, the speed/accuracy trade-off, 'N must be lower than the number of qubits' and the max-cut expectation-value mapping. There are still some things to fix. In [55], 'Pauli Hamiltonian' is written '해밀턴', which is the physicist Hamilton, not the operator; it should be '해밀토니안'. Entry [43] alone switches to '큐비트' and '3-local/N-local', while the rest of the file uses '큐빗' and 'N-로컬'. Entry [51] translates 'While' as a time clause ('~도움이 되는 동안'), which is a calque. The whole page uses the formal -습니다 style instead of the 해요체 convention the project expects.

examples.source: we require a Pauli Hamiltonian that encodes the cost
examples.translation: 비용을 인코딩하는 Pauli 해밀턴이 필요합니다
examples.suggested: 비용을 인코딩하는 Pauli 해밀토니안이 필요해요
examples.why: '해밀턴' is the person Hamilton; the standard Korean term for the operator is '해밀토니안'.

examples.source: acts on three qubits, making the circuit $3$-local ... $N$-local circuits
examples.translation: 3개의 큐비트에 작용하는 ... $3$-local로 만듭니다 ... $N$-local 회로
examples.suggested: 3개의 큐빗에 작용하는 ... $3$-로컬 회로가 돼요 ... $N$-로컬 회로
examples.why: The rest of the file uses '큐빗' and 'N-로컬'; this entry alone switches to '큐비트' and leaves 'local' in English.

examples.source: While heuristic and hardware efficient ansaetze help us to solve a problem in a naive way, we can use problem-specific knowledge
examples.translation: 휴리스틱 및 하드웨어 효율적인 ansatz가 문제를 순진한 방식으로 해결하는 데 도움이 되는 동안, 우리는 문제 특정 지식을 사용하여
examples.suggested: 휴리스틱 ansatz와 하드웨어 효율적인 ansatz는 문제를 단순한 방식으로 푸는 반면, 문제에 특화된 지식을 활용하면
examples.why: This 'while' is contrastive, but '~동안' reads as a time clause; '순진한' is also a literal calque of 'naive'.

examples.source: Otherwise, without at least one parameter, there wouldn't be any variations!
examples.translation: 그렇지 않으면 최소한 하나의 매개변수 없이는 어떤 변형도 없을 것입니다!
examples.suggested: 매개변수가 하나도 없으면 변분할 대상이 없으니까요!
examples.why: '그렇지 않으면' and '매개변수 없이는' say the same thing twice, which reads stiff and robotic.

examples.source: To learn about other strategies, refer to the TwoLocal documentation.
examples.translation: 다른 전략에 대해 알아보려면 ... 문서를 참조합니다.
examples.suggested: 다른 전략은 ... 문서를 참고하세요.
examples.why: This is a declarative '참조합니다' where an instruction to the reader is needed. More broadly, the whole file uses the formal -습니다 style instead of the 해요체 convention.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the variational-theorem derivation, the bounds caveats in [49]-[51], and the equality condition in [44]. The only departure is in [40], where 'higher than' becomes '높거나 같습니다'. That actually matches the ≥ in the math, so it does not mislead. Two things a native editor would still change. 'Expected energy' is calqued as '기댓값 에너지' in [30] and [40], where Korean physics writing uses '에너지 기댓값'. [22] also opens with an English-style subject, '우리는 문제를…'. Core terms are correct and consistent: 변분 알고리즘, 참조 상태, 변분 형식, 바닥 상태, 고유 상태, 관측량, 기댓값, with ansatz kept in English.

examples.source: the expected energy of a system in the (normalized) state $|\psi\rangle$ will be:
examples.translation: (정규화된) 상태 $|\psi\rangle$에 있는 시스템의 기댓값 에너지는 다음과 같이 계산됩니다.
examples.suggested: (정규화된) 상태 $|\psi\rangle$에 있는 시스템의 에너지 기댓값은 다음과 같습니다.
examples.why: '기댓값 에너지' copies the English word order. The standard Korean term is '에너지 기댓값'.

examples.source: the expected energy of any system is higher than the lowest energy or ground state energy
examples.translation: 임의의 시스템의 기댓값 에너지는 최저 에너지, 즉 바닥 상태 에너지보다 높거나 같습니다.
examples.suggested: 임의의 시스템의 에너지 기댓값은 최저 에너지, 즉 바닥 상태 에너지보다 높거나 같습니다.
examples.why: Same calque as in [30]. The added '같거나' follows the ≥ in the formula, so keep it.

examples.source: We can encode our problem into a _cost function_ $C(\vec\theta)$ as a linear combination of Pauli operators, run on a quantum system.
examples.translation: 우리는 문제를 Pauli 연산자의 선형 결합으로 표현된 _비용 함수_ $C(\vec\theta)$로 인코딩하여 양자 시스템에서 실행할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 문제를 Pauli 연산자의 선형 결합으로 표현된 _비용 함수_ $C(\vec\theta)$로 인코딩하여 양자 시스템에서 실행할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The explicit subject '우리는' carries over English syntax. Korean technical prose normally leaves it out.
